first.rationale: Onboarding deterioration is directly tied to the concurrent activation decline, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Promotional pricing is the strongest alternative given competitive pressure, but its archived record should be checked for retention, customer quality, and post-promotion revenue effects before preferring it for sustainable qualified revenue.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified prior test directly improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, aligning with both current declines and the sustainable qualified-revenue objective. Although promotional pricing addresses the competitive threat, its verified 12% retention decline and failure at first renewal make it unsuitable for this objective. An experiment rather than broad rollout preserves uncertainty about transferability to current users and conditions.
